critical_code_review_comments: 3-chain merge logic correctly reads _par_combined=True for L3's parent (L2) and propagates _par_root_bal/_par_root_date from L2's prev_opening_balance/prev_loan_date (which were set when L2 was merged with L1).

extra_kisht_entries accumulation: _par_extra + [{amount: _par_repayable, loan_date: _par_date}] correctly builds the chain list. For L3: L2's extra_kisht_entries=[] + L2's row = [{amount:24000, date:'2023-08-15'}].

chain_start merge pass (line 322-324): parent_strip[entry['month']]['status'] not in ('na', 'netoff') — 'chain_start' is NOT in the exclusion list, so L2's chain_start at 2023-08 propagates correctly into L3's FY strip.

chain_start injection for L3 at row_start_ym='2024-03': if entry is 'na' at that month, it's set to chain_start. Since L3 was disbursed in Mar 2024 with first EMI in Apr 2024 (next FY), Mar 2024 is 'na' → correctly becomes chain_start.
All 17 combined rows in FY 2025-26 have extra_kisht_entries field, confirming backward compatibility for 2-level chains (they get extra_kisht_entries=[]).

rca_of_issue: 3-chain merge works by iterating through loans in chronological order. When L3 processes its parent L2 (which is already is_netoff_combined=True from merging with L1): (1) _par_combined=True triggers the chain propagation path; (2) prev_opening_balance/prev_loan_date come from L2's prev_root values (L1's netoff amount + loan date); (3) extra_kisht_entries = L2's extras + L2's own entry = [{amount:24000, date:'2023-08'}]; (4) chain_start at L2's start month (2023-08) is preserved in merge because 'chain_start' status is not excluded like 'netoff'; (5) L3's own chain_start is injected at 2024-03 (L3's loan_date month which is 'na' in its own strip).
